references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Every food premises in Victoria is classified by the highest risk food handling it does. Class 1 serves potentially hazardous food to vulnerable people (hospitals, aged care, childcare). Class 2 handles unpackaged potentially hazardous food (most restaurants, cafes and takeaways). Class 3A makes hot-fill products such as chutney at home based or temporary premises. Class 3 handles unpackaged low risk food or stores and distributes pre-packaged food. Class 4 only does low risk activities such as selling pre-packaged low risk food, whole fruit and vegetables, or tea and coffee. Your registering council decides the class.
references.interpretation: A business that prepares or sells unpackaged food will be class 1, 2, 3 or 3A and must be registered with its council; a class 4 business only notifies council. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Class 2 premises must be registered under the Food Act 1984, have a nominated food safety supervisor and have a food safety program (with an annual audit, assessment or inspection depending on the program). Class 3 and 3A premises must be registered and are inspected annually; class 3A must have a food safety supervisor. Class 4 premises only notify their council.
references.interpretation: Registration applies to classes 1 to 3A; class 4 is notification only. Class 1 and 2 need a food safety program; class 1, 2 and 3A need a food safety supervisor. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.section: Who needs a food safety supervisor
references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Class 1, most class 2 and class 3A food premises must have a food safety supervisor who holds a Statement of Attainment from a registered training organisation in the units for their food sector (for example SITXFSA005 and SITXFSA006 for hospitality). Class 3 and 4 premises are exempt, as are some class 2 community groups trading for no more than 2 consecutive days.
references.interpretation: A cafe, restaurant or takeaway handling potentially hazardous food needs a trained food safety supervisor. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Temporary and mobile food premises such as food trucks, vans and market stalls apply online to their local council through the department's state-wide registration system, FoodTrader, which replaced Streatrader.
references.interpretation: A food van or stall registers once through FoodTrader with its principal council and then lodges statements of trade for each place it trades. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Council example: plans approval before construction (fee A$231.75 for classes 1 to 3), then the Food Act application and fee, classification by an Environmental Health Officer, progress and final inspections, then the certificate of registration. Registration fees depend on class and opening month (for example class 2 A$809.20 from January to June). Class 4 premises only notify council. Registration is renewed each calendar year.
references.interpretation: Shows the usual council process and order of magnitude of fees; each council sets its own fees. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] An on-premises licence lets you sell alcohol to drink at your venue without serving meals. Apply online through Service Victoria with proof of new entrant and RSA training, a red line plan, patron capacity and proof of right to occupy. The application goes to Victoria Police and council, you display a public notice for 28 days, and a decision takes about 9 to 11 weeks. Application fees are A$690.80 to A$863.20 depending on capacity. Staff serving alcohol need a current RSA certificate.
references.interpretation: Any business that sells or serves alcohol needs a licence or permit from Liquor Control Victoria; the type depends on the business. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] A restaurant and cafe licence is for venues where preparing and serving meals is the main activity at all times. Application fees are A$518.10 (0 to 200 customers), A$759.90 (201 to 400) or A$1,036.20 (401 or more). The same public notice and 9 to 11 week timeframe apply.
references.interpretation: Most cafes and restaurants that serve alcohol with meals apply for this licence. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.section: Outdoor dining and footpath trading permit
references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] A council permit is needed to place outdoor dining furniture, goods or A-frame signs on a footpath, road or other council land. Example (Hume City Council): General Purposes Local Law No. 1 2023, application fee A$226.00 (2025-26), permits expire on 31 August each year, and you must hold adequate public liability insurance.
references.interpretation: Using the footpath for tables, chairs, signs or goods needs a permit from the council under its local law; fees and rules differ by council. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Employers who employ workers in Victoria must register for WorkCover insurance with WorkSafe Victoria. You are exempt only if you have no apprentices and pay, or expect to pay, less than A$7,500 a year in remuneration.
references.interpretation: A business with employees must take out a WorkCover insurance policy unless it pays under A$7,500 a year in wages and has no apprentices. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.section: When a registered builder is needed
references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Domestic building work worth more than A$10,000, including labour, materials and GST, must be carried out by a builder registered with the Building and Plumbing Commission. Work by an unregistered builder over A$10,000 is not covered by domestic building insurance.
references.interpretation: A trade business that contracts for domestic building work over A$10,000 a job must be a registered domestic builder. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Domestic Builder (Unlimited) covers all components of domestic building work, possibly with conditions; Domestic Builder (Limited) classes cover particular work such as carpentry or glazing. You apply through BPC Online with a technical referee report from a builder registered in the same or a higher class.
references.interpretation: The class you need depends on the work you contract for. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] From 1 July 2026 Home Warranty applies to eligible domestic building work valued at more than A$20,000 on homes and residential buildings up to 3 storeys, unless an exclusion applies. Builders arrange it for each project through an approved distributor and pay the premium to get a Notice of Cover. Contracts signed before 1 July 2026 fall under domestic building insurance transitional arrangements.
references.interpretation: A registered builder taking on domestic building work over A$20,000 must arrange Home Warranty cover for each project before starting. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Plumbing work in Victoria must be done by a plumber registered or licensed with the Building and Plumbing Commission in the class of work. Registered plumbers can do the work but cannot supervise others or issue compliance certificates; a licensed plumber can supervise, issue compliance certificates (within 5 days of completing the work) and do design work. Registration lasts up to 3 years and a licence up to 12 months.
references.interpretation: A plumbing business needs at least one licensed plumber to issue compliance certificates for its work. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] A person or company in the business of electrical contracting, or offering to contract, must be a Registered Electrical Contractor (REC) with a business supervisor and a technical supervisor who holds a current Victorian electrician's licence, and at least A$5 million public liability insurance. Registration can be renewed for up to 5 years.
references.interpretation: An electrician working for customers needs an electrician's licence, and the business needs REC registration. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Licences are renewed every year. 2026-27 base renewal fees: restaurant and cafe A$391.70, on-premises A$1,327.50, general A$1,327.50, packaged liquor A$2,655.10, renewable limited A$391.70, plus risk fees for late trading, venue capacity and demerit points.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Employers in Victoria must register for and pay payroll tax when their Australian wages go over the threshold; ABLIS states a monthly threshold of A$75,000 from 1 July 2024 and a general rate of 4.85%, with a lower rate for regional employers. references.section: Registration of hair, beauty and body art businesses
references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Hair, beauty, tattoo and other personal care or body art businesses must register their premises with council under the Public Health and Wellbeing Act 2008 before opening. Registration is renewed each year, except that hairdressing and low risk beauty businesses (temporary make-up, henna, spray tans, lash and brow tinting) can choose a one-off ongoing registration that lasts until the business closes or changes owner. Council inspects the fit-out before issuing a registration certificate. A buyer of an existing business applies to transfer the registration.
references.interpretation: Any hair, beauty, tattooing, piercing or similar business needs council registration; only the renewal arrangement differs by risk. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Education and care services in Victoria under the Education and Care Services National Law are regulated by the Victorian Early Childhood Regulatory Authority (VECRA). Providers apply through the National Quality Agenda IT System (NQA ITS) with forms PA01 and PA02, criminal history checks, a Victorian Working with Children Check or VIT registration for each person with management or control, and the fee. A decision is due within 60 days of a complete application. Once a provider is approved, it applies for service approval in the state where the service will operate.
references.interpretation: Running long day care, kindergarten, outside school hours care or family day care in Victoria needs provider approval and service approval from VECRA. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] An imported vehicle needs import approval first. To register it in Victoria you need a current roadworthy certificate, the VIN recorded on the Register of Approved Vehicles (for example as Concessional - Vehicles modified by a RAW, Personal Effects or Older Vehicles) and stamped on the vehicle, and for vehicles built after 1968 a blue modification plate and VASS approval certificate. Complete the vehicle registration application form and book an appointment at a VicRoads Customer Service Centre. Vehicles less than 30 years old must be right-hand drive.
references.interpretation: Every imported road vehicle garaged in Victoria needs these documents before VicRoads will register it. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] To register a vehicle you need a completed vehicle registration form, evidence of identity, and a current original roadworthy certificate, and you bring the vehicle to the appointment for inspection. You pay an appointment fee, the registration charge, a number plate fee, the Transport Accident Commission (TAC) charge and motor vehicle duty.
references.interpretation: The registration appointment is where all charges, including the TAC charge and duty, are paid. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Generally, if you deal in four or more cars a year you need a motor car trader's licence from Consumer Affairs Victoria (sometimes fewer). You must be 18 or over, a fit and proper person, have lawful premises and know the Motor Car Traders Act 1986. You apply through myCAV. The combined application fee and first annual licence fee for 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027 is A$2,965.20.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] A boat, jet ski or e-foil that can use an engine for propulsion in Victorian waters must be registered. Vessels without a propulsion engine, recreational tenders and domestic commercial vessels are exempt, and some interstate vessels may be. You lodge the vessel registration form with evidence of identity, by post or at a Customer Service Centre, display the registration number on each side of the hull (at least 150 mm high, 100 mm for personal watercraft) and renew every 12 months.
references.interpretation: Any recreational vessel with an engine, whatever its power, needs Victorian registration; commercial vessels are dealt with by AMSA. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] To get a Victorian marine licence you pass an eyesight test and a 30 question knowledge test (26 correct to pass), based on the Victorian Recreational Boating Safety Handbook, at a VicRoads Customer Service Centre or an accredited training provider. A restricted marine licence is available from 12 years old. Operating a personal watercraft needs a PWC endorsement, which needs a separate 15 question test and is available from 16 years old.
references.interpretation: The person driving a registered recreational vessel needs a marine licence; a jet ski rider also needs a PWC endorsement. references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Grants help licensed hospitality venues improve security and fire suppression. rule_sets.title: Victoria: business licences and insurance
rule_sets.description: Food premises registration, food safety supervisors and programs, liquor licences, footpath trading, WorkCover insurance and payroll tax for Victorian businesses, from Safe Food Victoria, Department of Health, Liquor Control Victoria, WorkSafe Victoria, ABLIS and council pages.
limitations: Built from regulator, ABLIS and council web pages, not from the Food Act 1984, the Liquor Control Reform Act 1998 or the other Acts themselves.
Doesn't decide your food premises class; your council does. Meat, poultry, seafood and dairy businesses are licensed by Safe Food Victoria and aren't covered.
Doesn't decide which liquor licence type you need, or cover BYO permits, late night licences or packaged liquor in detail.
Footpath trading rules, fees and insurance amounts differ by council; only an example council was read.
Payroll tax is checked from staff numbers only; the current threshold couldn't be confirmed and grouping isn't checked.
Doesn't cover planning permits, building permits for a fit-out, signs or trade waste.
Not legal advice. Confirm with the regulator, your council or a qualified professional before you rely on it.

rules.title: Food premises registration (Food Act 1984)
rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-12), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: Register your food premises with your council
outcomes.detail: In Victoria, a business that makes food or sells unpackaged food must register its premises with the local council under the Food Act 1984 before it trades. Council puts you in a class from 1 (highest risk) to 4. Most cafes, restaurants and takeaways are class 2. Food vans and market stalls register through FoodTrader instead of a council form.

approval.pathway: Plans approval, registration, then a final inspection

evidence.title: Scaled floor plan and fit-out details
evidence.detail: Most councils want a 1:100 plan showing benches, sinks, hand basins, finishes and equipment before you build.

rules.title: Food vans and stalls: FoodTrader
rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-12), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: Register your food van or stall through FoodTrader
outcomes.detail: Food vans, trucks, carts and market stalls register online through FoodTrader, Victoria's state-wide system. Your principal council (usually where you garage or store the van) approves the registration. You then lodge a statement of trade in FoodTrader for each place and date you trade, anywhere in Victoria. Selling on a footpath, road or reserve also needs that council's permit.

rules.title: Food safety supervisor and food safety program
rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-12), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: Have a food safety supervisor and a food safety program
outcomes.detail: Class 1, most class 2 and class 3A premises must have a food safety supervisor with a Statement of Attainment from a registered training organisation (for cafes and restaurants, units SITXFSA005 and SITXFSA006). Class 1 and 2 premises also need a food safety program, which council checks each year. Food service businesses must also meet national Standard 3.2.2A (trained food handlers and, for many, records).

rules.title: Liquor licence (Liquor Control Victoria)
rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-12), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: You need a liquor licence from Liquor Control Victoria
outcomes.detail: Selling or serving alcohol in Victoria needs a licence or permit from Liquor Control Victoria. Cafes and restaurants where meals are the main activity usually need a restaurant and cafe licence; bars need an on-premises licence; bottle shops need a packaged liquor licence. Apply at least 11 weeks ahead: decisions take about 9 to 11 weeks and you must display a public notice for 28 days. You and your staff need RSA training.

rule_sets.title: Victoria: trade registrations and licences
rule_sets.description: Domestic builder registration and Home Warranty from the Building and Plumbing Commission, plumbing registration and licences, and electrical licences and contractor registration from Energy Safe Victoria.
limitations: Our question uses Queensland's A$3,300 job value; Victoria's builder registration threshold is A$10,000 and Home Warranty applies over A$20,000, so these findings are 'likely' rather than certain.
Doesn't cover commercial building practitioners, building surveyors, gas fitting, refrigeration (ARCtick) or asbestos removal.
Doesn't check which builder or plumbing class you need, or your qualifications.
Not legal advice. Confirm with the Building and Plumbing Commission or Energy Safe Victoria.

rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-12), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: You need to be a registered domestic builder for jobs over A$10,000
outcomes.detail: In Victoria, domestic building work worth more than A$10,000 a job (including labour, materials and GST) must be done by a builder registered with the Building and Plumbing Commission (BPC, formerly the VBA). Our question uses Queensland's A$3,300 limit, so if all your jobs are A$10,000 or less you don't need registration. Choose the class that covers your work: Domestic Builder (Unlimited) or a Limited class such as carpentry.
